title: Refused a meal at Takikawa Air Base and the MacArthur directive
summary: Officers deny the black troupe dinner at the officers' mess, so they cancel the show, nearly causing a riot, and MacArthur's office orders respectful treatment of USO shows.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: (We ran into it) (Unintelligible) up there. We left Tokyo too early to eat dinner. We got up there, the enlisted men had eaten and closed the dining room. What we did, we went to the officers' mess. That's where we usually ate, you know what I mean, the officers' mess. Officers sent us over to the enlisted men. So we go over there, and they had finished eating and cleaned up. So we came back to the theater and the G.I.s were just packed and jammed in there. So we called the group together and told them we were going back to Tokyo.
"We can't play on an empty stomach. If you don't think enough of us -- if officers are this --"
It was a lieutenant. It was a lieutenant that said, "No, we won't let you eat in the officers'
quarters." See, we were in the officers' wing.
(Unintelligible) rank of a captain, that's what we had.
And he said, " We're no blacks they didn't want us eating there. going to eat there." That was a set-up; (unintelligible). So we decided not to have a show. That's when they almost rioted, you know.

The G.I.'s almost rioted up there. So we got back in the trucks, we were riding in those big Army trucks, everybody had a little cushion, let's go back to Tokyo. That's what we did. The next day, hell popped loose. They issued a directive from MacArthur's office --
Stars and Stripes, all the newspapers.

That said, from now on, any unit that wanted a USO show had to treat them, with -- you know what I mean, with respect, you know what I mean. And they nipped that right in the bud, see. That never happened no more. Never happened again. But once in a while you run into that, you know.
